description:
Follow-up to fz-9x7.41.4 (I4). User (verbatim, relayed by GC 2026-11-20): "we should shore up the gaps in I4, if they're necessary to continue." Does not block I5 or the fz-9x7.11 collector steps; filed at the end of the epic.

Rust enters receive dispatch bodies with the process as an ordinary argument, not in the pinned register emit_place reads, so their boxes still call fz_box_*_for_any. ring makes 300,000 of them (~6M instructions, ~0.65% of ring). First step, on paper: should emit_place take the body's process value, or should the bodies enter with the process pinned? Related: fz-nml.9.5 (receive dispatch reuses native guard lowering). Owner: GC.

comments.text: Closes against fz-9x7.44.9 (No value is the address of a number); listed in that page's removal ledger. GC holds it.

title: A box made in a receive dispatch body is placed inline
